title: Wild Rice, 100% Cooked, No Added Fat

content.title: About
content.content: Wild rice is the seed of aquatic grasses native to North America. Despite its name, it is not a true rice but a grain with a nutty flavor and firm texture. This version is cooked without any added fat, steamed and ready to eat.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Wild rice contains more protein than conventional white rice.
It is rich in antioxidants such as ferulic and quercetin acids.
Indigenous peoples of the Pacific Northwest harvested wild rice for thousands of years.
Wild rice has been part of human diets for over 5,000 years.
Its golden hue after cooking earned it the nickname “golden grain.”

items.title: High protein content
items.content: Wild rice provides about 14 g of protein per 100 g, making it a solid plant‑based protein source.

items.title: Rich in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestion and promotes satiety.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Its glycemic index is lower than most white rice varieties, helping to stabilize blood sugar.

items.title: Source of magnesium and zinc
items.content: These minerals are essential for nerve function and immune health.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Phytonutrients protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to wild rice.

items.title: Phytic acid content
items.content: Phytic acid can reduce mineral absorption; soaking or fermenting can mitigate this.

items.title: Sodium in seasoned versions
items.content: If the rice is pre‑seasoned, watch sodium intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cooked wild rice can be served as a side dish with meat, fish or vegetables, tossed into salads, soups, and casseroles, or used as a grain substitute in vegetarian meals.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the cooked wild rice in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 4‑5 days. For longer storage, freeze portions in freezer‑safe bags.
